PLAN PATTERN

All-electric commercial space-heating plan

FIG. 01 — SCHEMATIC

Visual representation of All-electric commercial space-heating plan mechanics.

The Short Answer: All-electric commercial space-heating plan is separate designs exist for premises heating with electricity, and eligibility usually depends on the heating system rather than business type. On a commercial bill, this line typically indicates rightsize plan exposure.

FIG. 02 — STRUCTURAL CONTEXT

Why Utilities Use This Model

This rate design is intentionally structured by regulatory commissions to incentivize specific customer behaviors. By pricing electricity differently based on tou parameters, utilities aim to flatten the overall grid load and defer the need for building new power plants.

🧮 Worked Scenario

If your facility has a peak demand of 50kW and your tariff charges $10/kW (typical for a LOW band), that single line item costs you $500/month, regardless of how many kWh you actually use.

FIG. 03 — COMMON ERRORS

The Common Misread

The most common mistake is assuming owners assume a heat-labelled rate is automatically cheaper for their load shape. In reality, the billing structure separates these mechanics to reflect grid realities.

How to spot this: Check the top right corner of your bill for "Rate Schedule" or "Service Classification." Common codes include "GS-2", "E-19", or "Large TOU".

🎯 Your One Action This Week

Focus on rightsize plan. Review your last two bills to see if this specific lever is driving your costs.
